comment_corrections: /** Structural bindings are transient; breaking a part returns only the part itself. */
/** Base structural-part drop; the final drop mixin handles attached cover data separately. */

/** * GT6 physical hazard classes - acid, gas and plasma - as pure functions, plus the proof-flag * truth table used by existing vessels. Magic is classified separately by isMagic for pipe ticks. * *

Where GT6 keeps the answer. Not on the block and not on the pipe: every GT6 hazard test * is {@code FL.acid}/{@code FL.gas}/{@code FL.plasma} against a fluid name held in a global * set ({@code gregapi/data/CS.java:1508 FluidsGT}): *

    *
  • {@code FL.java:756} {@code acid(Fluid)} = {@code FluidsGT.ACID.contains(name)},
    • *
  • {@code FL.java:760} {@code plasma(Fluid)} = {@code FluidsGT.PLASMA.contains(name)},
    • *
  • {@code FL.java:770} {@code gas(Fluid)} = {@code !FluidsGT.LIQUID.contains(name) && * (fluid.isGaseous() || FluidsGT.GAS.contains(name))}.
    • *
* Those sets are filled at fluid-creation time, and the two rules behind them are different in kind: *
    *
  • gas and plasma are the fluid's physical state - {@code FL.java:1105} adds every fluid * created with {@code STATE_GASEOUS} to {@code FluidsGT.GAS}, {@code FL.java:1106} every * {@code STATE_PLASMA} fluid to {@code FluidsGT.PLASMA}, and {@code FL.java:1104} every * {@code STATE_LIQUID} fluid to {@code FluidsGT.LIQUID} (which is what makes the {@code gas()} * test subtract liquids);
    • *
  • acid is a material property, not a state - {@code FL.java:1118} adds the fluid to * {@code FluidsGT.ACID} when its {@code OreDictMaterial} carries {@code TD.Properties.ACID} * ({@code TD.java:386}), and {@code MT.java:121-126} is what puts it there for the * {@code gasacid*}/{@code lqudacid*} factories. So an acid can be a gas and a liquid at once: * hydrogen chloride is {@code gasaciddcmp} ({@code MT.java:1020}) and is in both sets.
    • *
* That is why {@link #isAcid}, {@link #isGas} and {@link #isPlasma} are three independent * predicates and GT6 tests them one after another ({@code MultiTileEntityPipeFluid.java:296}, * {@code :302}, {@code :308}) instead of switching on a single category. {@link #kindOf} exists for * callers that want one answer and documents its precedence. * *

How the port answers the same questions. The port keeps the GT6 metadata on * {@link RegisteredFluids.FluidEntry} instead of in name sets: {@link RegisteredFluids.FluidEntry#gas()} * is the {@code STATE_GASEOUS} bit and {@link RegisteredFluids.FluidFlags#PLASMA} the * {@code STATE_PLASMA} bit, both resolved for a live {@link Fluid} through * {@link GTFluids#entryForFluid} - which also resolves the {@code _flowing} variant, so a flowing gas * is classified like its still fluid. The acid property survives on the material, so it is read back * with {@link FluidVisualPolicy#material} (the same {@code materialKey} / {@code boundMaterial} * resolution the renderer uses) and tested against {@link MaterialProperty#ACID}, which the port * already fills for GT6's acid materials ({@code MaterialFormCorrections.java:45-52}, the same list * {@code FL.java:1118} derives from {@code TD.Properties.ACID}). * *

This class is deliberately stateless and cache-free: every method is a registry lookup plus a * comparison, so the per-tick callers below can call it on the hot path. The acid branch is the only * one that has to resolve a material, and {@link #proofRejects(Fluid, boolean, boolean, boolean)} * short-circuits it away for any vessel that is already acid proof. * * @see #proofRejects(Fluid, boolean, boolean, boolean) the accept/reject decision the vessels use */

/** * Registry-backed fluid hazard queries shared by vessel and pipe callers. * Acid comes from the resolved material; plasma and declared gas state come from fluid metadata. * Magic also has a material fallback in {@link #isMagic}; individual callers may use narrower rules. * *

Original predicates are FL.acid/gas/plasma/magic and the FluidsGT name sets. * Unknown modern fluids use the native lighter-than-air approximation for gas; it does not * reproduce the old independent isGaseous flag. These queries depend on the live registry. */

/** * GT6 {@code FL.java:770} {@code FL.gas}: the fluid's own state is {@code STATE_GASEOUS} * ({@code FL.java:1105}). * *

For a fluid with no GT6 declaration the {@code FluidsGT.GAS} name set cannot answer, so the * question falls to Forge's own lighter-than-air flag, which is the 1.20.1 equivalent of the * {@code fluid.isGaseous()} half of GT6's test. GT6's {@code !FluidsGT.LIQUID.contains(name)} guard * is already encoded in the port's metadata: {@code withGas()} clears * {@link RegisteredFluids.FluidFlags#LIQUID}, so {@code entry.gas()} cannot be true for a declared * liquid. * *

{@code Fluids.EMPTY} is never a gas: it has no GT6 declaration, and Forge's empty fluid type * reports {@code isLighterThanAir()} — so the fallback has to exclude it explicitly, or "no fluid" * would count as a breathable gas (the gate caught exactly that). */

/**
     * Declared GT gas state takes precedence. Unknown nonempty fluids fall back to the native
     * lighter-than-air flag, which is an approximation of the original independent gas predicate.
     * Empty fluid is excluded because its native type can report lighter than air.
     */

readability.limit: Whitespace, two local id bindings renamed registryId, and three source-backed documentation corrections only. No gameplay changes.

finite_source_witnesses.kind: Finite source predicates/counts, not execution of target classes or world behavior.

wood_valve.current: TankControllerBlock has no override; registered through metal factory properties, native fire-table fallback has no GT valve registration in the examined production tree.
wood_valve.wood_wall: 18001 is already explicitly 150 through Part.flammability -> MultiblockPortBlock; not missing.

meltdown_neighbour.original: WD.burn(F,F) -> WD.fire: excludes lava/fire, accepts carpet or no collision; honors old IItemGT/Thaumcraft node checks before unconditional branch.
meltdown_neighbour.current: Requires loaded, not FIRE, empty fluid state and empty collision shape before setting fire.

finite_cases.neighbour: loaded nonlava fluid with no collision, no GT/node exclusion

meltdown_neighbour.policy: Keep modern loaded/fluid protection; do not silently expand destructive effects. A setBlock attempt does not prove sustained fire in a world.

finite_source_witnesses.lava: Only size3, vanilla lava/flowing lava and at least1000; size5 has no lava-pool branch. No extra fluid acceptance or explosion proved.

ordinary_transfer.limit: No 1000 throttle in either source branch; adversarial callback atomicity and native side integration not runtime-tested.

unaccepted_property_edges: Tank magic branch reads explicit MAGIC while helper isMagic also resolves MAGICAL; material import flags and real surviving low-temperature examples need separate acceptance.
Unknown add-on gas uses native lighter-than-air approximation rather than legacy independent isGaseous; no concrete add-on integration accepted.
Original optional Flux block replacement differs when that integration is present; default unavailable Flux cannot be treated as mandatory pollution in the modern baseline.
excluded_false_positives: Wooden wall already has fire metadata.
Meltdown/magic/acid/plasma/gas/simple restrictions already have tick branches.
Generated molten entries use material melting temperature; do not label them all ambient from the declaration helper default.
Steam explicitly uses373K in both sources.
Auto-output formula matches all36 selected direction/gas/density inputs; no1000 throttle exists.

limits: No Java compilation/initialization, Gradle, tests, game, build or push.
